                   Public Utility Commission of Texas

                                     Memorandum


 TO:            Interested Persons

 FROM:          Jessie Horn, Sr. Counsel, Rules and Projects Division

 DATE:          January 2, 2026

 RE:            Project No. 58484, Rulemaking to Implement Large Load Interconnection
                Standards Under PURA §37.0561


Commission staff will hold a public workshop on January 9, 2026. The workshop will be held
in Room 2.035 on the second floor of the Barbara Jordan State Office Building, 1601 Congress
Avenue, Austin, Texas 78701. The Barbara Jordan State Office Building’s entrance is located
off of the Texas Capitol Mall, a pedestrian walkway. A map of the Texas Capitol Complex is
included as Attachment A to this memorandum for reference. The workshop will also be
broadcast live and archived for later viewing on Admin Monitor, which can be accessed at:
https://www.adminmonitor.com/tx/puct/.

The purpose of the workshop is to receive public input on topics related to Project No. 58481,
Rulemaking to Implement Large Load Interconnection Standards Under PURA §37.0561. The
workshop will begin at 9:30 a.m.

The format for the workshop will be open discussion guided by commission staff’s questions
for comment, included as Attachment B to this memorandum. A second discussion draft is
included as Attachment C to this memorandum. Additionally, a process flow chart is included
as Attachment D to this memorandum.

                                                                       ATTACHMENT B
                                                             QUESTIONS FOR COMMENT


1. Should the rule define “dynamic modeling” for large loads? If so, what definition should
   be used?
2. If the commission includes an “initial screening study” as an option that a large load
   customer may request from an interconnecting utility prior to the initiation of a large load
   interconnection study, how should the commission define “initial screening study”?
       a. What specific and preliminary information would an initial screening study need to
          identify for a large load customer to determine whether a site is feasible?
       b. What specific and preliminary information would the interconnecting utility need
          from the large load customer to perform an initial screening study?
       c. Should a fee be imposed on a large load customer for the interconnecting utility to
          conduct an initial screening study? If so, what amount should be used for a
          standardized initial screening study fee?
       d. What is an appropriate time frame for an interconnecting utility to complete an
          initial screening study?
       e. How would this initial screening study differ from today’s current processes?
3. Should the commission maintain the definition for an interconnecting utility that is set forth
   in Attachment C? If not, what definition should be used?
4. If the commission maintains the definition for an interconnecting utility that is set forth in
   Attachment C, what framework should the rule establish for ensuring that the
   interconnecting transmission service provider receives the required security and CIAC in
   instances where the certificated retail utility and interconnecting transmission service
   provider are different entities?
5. For a large load customer that seeks to expand capacity at an existing site, should the total
   capacity or only the new incremental capacity at that site be subject to the rule
   requirements? Why?
6. Currently, ERCOT Planning Guide §9.2.1(1)(b) requires a large load customer to follow
   the criteria subject to the large load interconnection study process if the large load customer
   modifies an existing load facility that increases the aggregate peak demand of the facility
   by 75 MW or more. Should the commission maintain this threshold for purposes of the
   rule? Or should any modification that increases the aggregate peak demand of the facility
   to 75 MW or more be required to satisfy the criteria in the rule?
7. Does an interconnecting utility, at the intermediate agreement phase, have sufficient
   information to be able to estimate the costs of significant equipment and services and to
   estimate contribution in aid of construction?
       a. If so, should the rule require payment of the $100,000 per megawatt security at the
          time the request for interconnection is submitted? And require estimated security
          for significant equipment and services and contribution in aid of construction at the
          intermediate agreement stage, subject to a true up based on actual costs identified
          at the interconnection agreement stage?
                                                                        ATTACHMENT B
                                                              QUESTIONS FOR COMMENT
8. Should the commission expand the criteria for demonstrating site control to include either
   site control over an electrical substation combined with exclusive development rights at a
   designated interconnection point or an exclusivity agreement with an existing generation
   resource for a proposed net metering arrangement?
9. What value may be gained from collecting data about project developers and end-use
   customers for purposes of developing ERCOT’s load forecasts?
10. How should an interconnecting utility treat interest accrued from cash security?
       a. What interest rate should apply?
       b. What process should be used to return interest to the large load customer?
11. What is the average CIAC that is charged to a large load customer seeking to interconnect
    today?
12. For what period of time should a large load customer be expected to operate after
    energization but before the interconnecting utility issues a final refund of any unused
    security, collateral, or CIAC in order to balance the state’s interests in supporting business
    development and minimizing the potential for stranded infrastructure costs?
13. If the commission adopts a process whereby ERCOT, not the interconnecting utility,
    reallocates capacity on a system-wide basis through a batch study process, what parameters
    should the commission establish for such a process?
14. Is 60 days a sufficient time frame for an interconnecting utility to issue a required refund?
15. What changes should be made to Attachment C to account for the fact that municipally
    owned utilities and electric cooperatives have exclusive jurisdiction over retail rates in their
    service territory?
16. Is there anything else that the commission should consider in its implementation of PURA
    §37.0561?

 3         a municipally owned utility, and electric cooperative, to interconnect a large load customer

 4         to the ERCOT transmission network.

 7         meanings unless the context indicates otherwise:

 8         (1)    Backup generating facilities -- Generation facilities that are not capable of

 9                exporting energy to the ERCOT transmission system and that, in aggregate, can

10                serve at least 50% of on-site contracted peak demand.

15                financing structures.   Competitively sensitive information does not include the

17                timing of energization; or whether an interconnection request is associated with the

18                same applicant or affiliated entities.

20                requests that an interconnecting utility serve at a site as stated in an executed and

21                securitized intermediate agreement or interconnection agreement.
